claims.text: Preheating the build substrate to approximately 500°C during SLM of CoCrFeMnNi will reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients will mitigate residual stresses.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stresses will minimize fabrication-induced defects.
Substrate preheating will improve dimensional precision relative to fabrication on an unheated substrate.
Substrate preheating will improve mechanical integrity relative to fabrication on an unheated substrate.
Reducing thermal gradients across the melt pool and substrate will produce more uniform solidification.
Elevating the substrate temperature reduces the temperature differential between the molten pool and build platform.
The reduced temperature differential diminishes rapid cooling.
Thermal-profile stabilization lowers the likelihood of hot cracking.
Thermal-profile stabilization lowers porosity.
Thermal-profile stabilization lowers warping.
Thermal-profile stabilization results in a more uniform microstructure.
A more uniform microstructure supports improved dimensional fidelity.
A more uniform microstructure supports robust mechanical properties.
Preheated samples will have fewer microcracks and less porosity than the unheated baseline.
Preheated samples will have a finer grain structure than the unheated baseline.
Preheated samples will have higher tensile strength than the unheated baseline.
Preheated samples will have higher ductility than the unheated baseline.
Under unheated-substrate conditions, high thermal gradients cause pronounced residual stresses and dimensional inaccuracies.

The intervention is expected to apply under standard inert-atmosphere SLM conditions for CoCrFeMnNi with fixed laser parameters, but may vary with alloy composition, geometry, and extreme processing conditions.
